steps.title: Priestley's Vision
steps.body: "An Inspector Calls" argues for exactly these changes. Inspector's final speech - "we are members of one body" - advocates the social solidarity that led to the welfare state.

steps.title: The Inspector as Socialist Voice
steps.body: Inspector's final speech is pure socialist message. He argues that privilege brings responsibility, that we must care for each other, that ignoring the vulnerable has consequences.

steps.title: "An Inspector Calls" - Genre Blend
steps.body: Starts as realistic drawing-room drama, becomes expressionist. The Inspector seems supernatural. Time is distorted. These theatrical choices make the audience think beyond realism.

steps.title: Context Must Be Integrated, Not Bolted On
steps.body: Examiners award AO3 marks for context that is woven into your argument, not dumped in a separate paragraph. Always link historical, social, or political context directly to the writer's choices and the text's meaning. A disconnected "life in 1912" paragraph scores poorly; a sentence that explains why Priestley chose 1912 to create dramatic irony scores highly.
